title: Yields Scream Higher, Gold And Silver At Pivot Break Point: $3,500 And $50 Odds Increase!
speaker: Gareth Soloway

macro_themes.view: 10y near 5.35%, above the 2007 peak; a confirmed close above opens 5.5%, driven by strong economy and global debt/unrest, not inflation.
Strong earnings, global capital fleeing to the US and a strong economy keep stocks rising despite high yields and oil; upside into midterms and year-end, issues in 2027.
A strong economy should make silver outperform gold; long-term bull on gold due to fiscal irresponsibility everywhere.

calls.condition: If the 10y closes above the 2007 peak with confirmation, expect a move to 5.5%
calls.reason: Weekly chart: yields above the 2007 peak, highest since 2002; continuing higher after the jobs-report dip.
calls.quote: if we close above this level, especially with confirmation, I would insinuate or expect a move up to the 5.5% level on yields

calls.condition: Bullish above ~7,575; neutral zone 7,400-7,575; below ~7,400 he exits longs and goes heavily short
calls.reason: Holding above his bullish line; trend-line target near 8,000; upside through midterms into year-end before 2027 issues.
calls.quote: It's right around 8,000 currently sneaking up slowly, and that's where I think we are headed.

calls.condition: If gold breaks the trend line at ~4,100, target 3,950-3,960; if 3,950 breaks, 3,500, where he would buy
calls.reason: Bear flag hammering a trend line from May 2025; rising yields pressure gold; long-term bull on fiscal irresponsibility.
calls.quote: if it breaks 3950, which was the previous low on the last dip, it is going down to 3500

calls.condition: If silver breaks its long-term trend line, support 54-55; below that, toward just under $50 (possibly $48)
calls.reason: Sitting on a longer-term trend line; just below $50 is the 1980/2011 high and his buy level; industrial demand helps it vs gold in a strong economy.
calls.quote: If it breaks that, you're likely headed down to this pivot just below 50.

notes: Date inferred: host says jobs data was 'last Friday', ISM services 'this morning' and the S&P is up today, i.e. Monday 2026-10-05 (listing says 10-06). Gold/silver bearish calls are conditional on trend-line breaks; long-term bias bullish for both (silver long-term implied from 'overall long-term bull'). Gold price at call not stated (just above 4,100 implied).
